posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
The big difference between Sentinels and any CCG is that in a CCG you look at the card lists to see what cards work with your deck, and get ideas for your new decks.

 

If a Magic expansion was a box of decks that you did not customize they wouldn't post the cards, they'd post pictures of the deck's theme, and give a description, maybe a card or two to highlight the deck.

 

In SotM they post hero bios.  You get a feel for what the deck will be like, and it builds excitement to play the hero, or you say, "I don't think I'll like that hero, but this one over here sounds fun."

 

A complete card list helps a few situations:  

1.  Someone has a toddler named William, and that Toddler gets into their box and now Parse has 39 cards and they have no clue where that card went, or what card is even missing.

2.  Reference when talking about cards online and you decks are harder to access than an online list.

3.  When you think of something really cool you want to try with Hero A and Hero B and you can't remember the exact text of the cards and you are at work so you can't get out your cards, or even focus because it is driving you crazy.

 

It will not help promote the game.

It will not be a big part of getting new players into the game.

It will be convenient for current players, and those waiting for their game to get to them and are desperate for spoilers.

posts.name: e.hananto
posts.cooked:
Just to offer personal anecdote, in the past I had purchased games after I obsessively looked at their card spoiler so to me it certainly play a big role on promoting the game to me. IMO Sentinels big points lie on the intricate card interactions and brand new players have no way of seeing that short of looking at the card text (or playing off someone's copy obviously). Yes you can read heroes fluff and get an idea of how they play, but without seeing the proper context of card interaction, new potential players will not have any idea on how it could play out.

Yes SotM is not a CCG, but even other LCG game which come with fixed deck have full spoilers somewhere and they greatly help on convincing existing players to buy a particular set, though admitedly they are also not hosted from the official site so probably the same situation as what we have now. 

I understand your stands Lynkfox and certainly respects your position. And I still would love to see it happen, so perhaps when the time allow I'll will try to see if I can get it going on wikispace or wikia (hated wikia excessive ad though), and I agree with the bandwidth limitation point so I also think it's best to start with just the text spoiler.

 

Edit: With the full image spoilers I don't even think print & play is a feasible idea, for one the low resolution will make it looks really ugly when printed, and when you add up the cost of printing full colour + the trouble off proper cutting, you are much better off buying the game. Even if you send it to a printer studio (eg. artscow) for printing, with that huge number of cards in the end it's still cheaper to just buy the game.

People may print-and-play the game and have one free copy, sure.  It's unlikely someone would do that if they had any intention of buying the game proper.  It doesn't save money, look better, or store better if printed on card stock or sleeved with proxy cards.  But what happens if someone else plays this print and play game and wants a copy?  Will they print it all out themselves?  Possibly.  But they might also just buy the game.  As far as I'm concerned it is at least somewhat likely that money will be gained from releasing that spoiler.

I've just noticed that Greater Than Games has said nothing against a full card spoiler, but has expressed some limitations on what exactly they want released to the public as spoilers for future sets.  End of the day?  The wiki is your baby and you can do what you please with it.  It has already been an excellent resource, and a lack of a spoiler list won't diminish it in any way.  Though your preference is not necessarily opposite of Greater Than Games, it does seem to have some noteworthy differences.
